query: Lee Jae-myung approval rating Gallup Korea Realmeter late June early July 2026, is approval still falling, what is driving the decline, any dead cross
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings on Lee Jae-myung's approval ratings for late June/early July 2026:

**Is approval still falling?** The sustained multi-week slide **bottomed out in late June 2026** and has partially recovered in July, though the two main trackers now diverge slightly.

**Gallup Korea:** Fell to a record low of **51%** on June 26 (disapproval 41%), rebounded to **54%** on July 3, then edged down to **52%** by July 17 (two straight small weekly declines).

**Realmeter:** Fell for six consecutive weeks; recorded the **"dead cross" on June 22** (approval 46.7% vs. disapproval 49.7% — first time disapproval exceeded approval since inauguration), continued to 46.5% on June 29, then **rose two straight weeks to 48.9%** by July 13, reversing the dead cross.

**Dead cross:** Occurred **only in Realmeter** (June 22–29), and was reversed by mid-July. Gallup never recorded one.

**What drove the decline:** (1) National Election Commission election-management controversy, (2) real-estate/housing policy and tightened mortgage lending amid Seoul home-price surges, (3) economy/livelihood concerns, (4) ruling Democratic Party infighting, and earlier (May) concerns over "excessive" welfare spending.

**What drove the July rebound:** The "three megaprojects" initiative (semiconductors, physical AI, AI data centers, unveiled June 29) and positive diplomacy sentiment (NATO Defense Industry Forum).

key_facts: Gallup Korea: Lee's approval hit a record post-inauguration low of 51% on June 26, 2026 (down 6pp), with disapproval reaching 41% — the first time disapproval hit the 40% range.
Realmeter recorded a 'dead cross' on June 22, 2026: approval 46.7% (−4.8pp) vs. disapproval 49.7% (+5.5pp) — the first time disapproval exceeded approval since inauguration.
Realmeter approval fell for six consecutive weeks, reaching 46.5% on June 29, 2026 (second week in the 40s).
Approval rebounded in July: Gallup rose to 54% on July 3, 2026 (+3pp), aided by the 'three megaprojects' announcement.
Realmeter rose for two straight weeks to 48.9% by July 13, 2026 (+1.9pp), with approval back above disapproval (47.7%), driven by diplomacy.
Latest Gallup reading (July 17, 2026) edged down to 52% (−1pp), a second consecutive small weekly decline.
Key decline drivers cited: NEC election-management controversy, real-estate/housing policy and tightened lending, economy/livelihood concerns, and ruling Democratic Party infighting.
Gallup never recorded a dead cross; Realmeter's dead cross was reversed by mid-July 2026.
Realmeter peak was a post-inauguration high of 65.5% in early April 2026; Gallup peaked around 64–65% in early 2026.
Party support (Gallup, June 26, 2026): Democratic Party 41%, People Power Party 27%.
